title: Asiya in Pharaoh's house
hook: Pharaoh's wife, who kept faith in the harshest house (66:11)

segments.voice: Yesterday: Maryam, and your line, named. Today, a woman the Qur'an never names, and sets beside Maryam anyway.

A hard address for a person of faith: not a desert, not a prison, but a palace. The palace of the man who declared himself lord most high, who had the baby boys of a whole people killed. And inside it, married to him, a woman who believed. The Qur'an calls her only the wife of Pharaoh. Tradition gives her the name Asiya. She first appears when a chest is pulled out of the river.

Surah al-Qasas tells it. Pharaoh's household pulls a baby out of the river, the baby Musa. In a house that kills boys, his wife speaks first: he'll be a comfort of the eye for me and for you, don't kill him; maybe he'll be useful to us, or we'll take him as a son. Her first recorded words save a prophet's life. In surah sixty-six she speaks again, and this time it's a prayer. In Pickthall's translation: "My Lord! Build for me a home with Thee in the Garden." She goes on to ask to be saved from Pharaoh and his deeds, and from a wrongdoing people. The Qur'an sets her up as an example for all believers, and in the next verse sets Maryam beside her: one in a palace, one under a palm. Notice the order of her words in Arabic: rabbi-bni li 'indaka baytan fil-jannah. 'Indaka, with You, comes before baytan, a house. Some scholars sum that detail up with an old saying: the neighbor before the house. What happened to her, the Qur'an doesn't say. Commentators tell stories of her suffering for her faith; those come from later reports, not from the verse. What the hadith does say, in al-Bukhari, is that many men reached perfection, but among women only Maryam and Asiya, the wife of Pharaoh. The Qur'an never shows her leaving that house. It shows her keeping her faith inside it, and saving a child while she was there.

Think of the place in your life that's hardest to be good in, a job, a family table, a group chat, somewhere you can't simply walk out of. Ask what one small thing you could protect there, the way Asiya protected a baby: a kind word, a boundary, a quiet prayer, someone weaker than you. If you pray, you can say her line: my Lord, build for me a home with You.
Asiya. Pharaoh's believing wife, who saved the baby Musa and prayed for a home with Allah, with You before the house. Today's word.
Your line: faith in pharaoh's house. With You first, then the house. See you tomorrow.

howItsDone: Muslims honor Asiya, with Maryam, as a woman the hadith says reached perfection; her prayer in 66:11 is learned and recited as a du'a, including in hardship.
